tagline.text: A national park around the 2.8 km Colapnitan Cave and its bats

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (per person, including transport from Naga and a guide)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Naga Airport (WNP) or Bicol International Airport (DRP)

children.text: Libmanan Caves National Park is a 19.4-hectare limestone protected area in Barangay Sigamot, Libmanan, Camarines Sur. Clustered around the roughly 2.8 km Colapnitan Cave, it is an adventure destination best visited with a guide after confirming current conditions with the local tourism office.

Libmanan Caves National Park is a protected area in Barangay Sigamot, Libmanan, in Camarines Sur province of the Bicol region. It was established on February 6, 1934, under Proclamation No. 654, and covers about
19.4 hectares
. It is managed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and falls under IUCN Category III (natural monument). The nearest large city is Naga, and the park lies about
15km
from Libmanan town proper.

The heart of the park is Colapnitan Cave (also spelled Culapnitan locally). Wikipedia and several local guides give its length as about 2,856 m and describe it as the tenth longest cave in the Philippines. In the gentle hills and farmland around it, at least 18 more limestone caves of various sizes are said to exist. Cave names mentioned in local write-ups include Alinsanay, Balinsasayaw, Binubon, Kalangkawan, and Taros-taros.

Thousands of bats live inside, and their guano has been harvested for decades. Swiftlets and Phrynus whip spiders are also said to live there. With stalactites, stalagmites, and massive limestone pillars in a dark, damp cave, this is not a developed tourist cave; treat it as an adventure trip to be done with a guide and proper gear.

One caveat first. A blog post based on the local tourism office reported that, due to poor management, many trails are blocked by fallen trees, most caves are no longer accessible, and a visit is not recommended in the current state. More recent travel guides, on the other hand, list entrance fees and explain how to book a guide, implying visitors are accepted. Because the accounts conflict, be sure to check with the Libmanan Tourism Office and the local DENR office before you go.
The core of the park, this cave is about 2.8 km long and is described as the tenth longest in the Philippines. You can see large chambers, stalactites, and stalagmites. Some guides suggest allowing
2–4 hours
to explore it.
Thousands of bats live in the cave. The sight of bats flying out of the cave at dusk is described as its signature scene. Keep your distance so you do not disturb the bats or the nesting birds.

Stalactites, stalagmites, and thick limestone columns, formed as water slowly dissolved the limestone over a long time, line the cave. Touching them can halt their growth or damage them, so look with your eyes and keep your hands off.

Caves with names such as Alinsanay, Balinsasayaw, Binubon, Kalangkawan, and Taros-taros are said to lie in and around the park. Some are meant for experienced cavers and it is easy to get lost, and whether they are accessible can change from time to time.

Forest trails run through the hills around the cave, and guides mention Philippine macaques, monitor lizards, wild boars, and various birds and butterflies. You can also explore just the surroundings without entering the cave.

It became a national park under Proclamation No. 654 in 1934, relatively early for the Philippines. The designation was meant to protect the area's geology and cave environment, and today it is managed by DENR as a protected area.

Libmanan also has natural attractions such as Engkanto Falls (a stream of about 20 small cascades), Tinandayagan Falls, Malinao Springs, and island hopping. Many travelers combine the caves with these for a one-day itinerary.

items.title: Day trip from Naga
items.subtitle: Exploring Colapnitan Cave with a guide

children.text: Board a jeepney or bus bound for Libmanan at the SM Naga terminal in Naga City. A rental car or a car with a driver is more comfortable.
Arrive in Libmanan town proper, confirm your arrangement with the tourism office, and double-check the access situation and your guide. Take a tricycle to the park.
Pay the entrance fee at the park entrance in Barangay Sigamot and confirm your helmet and guide. Switch on your headlamp and follow the guide into Colapnitan Cave.
Come out of the cave and eat the packed lunch you brought. There is reportedly no food for sale in or around the cave, so prepare your meals in advance.
Walk the forest trails or head to a nearby waterfall, then return to town before sunset and catch transport back to Naga.
Guides list the evening bat flight as a highlight of this cave but warn against exploring caves at night. Arrange your transport for after dark in advance.
Leave Naga and arrive in Libmanan.
Explore a short section of the cave with a guide at Libmanan Caves National Park.
Return to town for lunch.
Pick one nearby attraction, such as Engkanto Falls (Barangay Bical) or Tinandayagan Falls. Check access and entry arrangements locally.
Head back to Naga.

Waterfalls swell in the rainy season, but the paths become slippery. When combining a waterfall with the cave on the same day, finish the cave in the morning and skip the waterfall if rain is forecast.
You can take an overnight bus from Manila (PITX, Pasay, Alabang, and others) to the Bicol Central Terminal in Naga City. One outlet put the ride at about
10–11 hours
You can also fly from Manila to Naga Airport (WNP) or Bicol International Airport (DRP) and continue overland. Check the airline for schedules and fares.
Manila to Libmanan is about 363 km, and one news report put the drive at around
8–9 hours
by private car.
Take a jeepney or bus bound for Libmanan at the SM Naga terminal in Naga City. The trip is said to take about
1 hour
. Confirm the fare before boarding.
From Libmanan town proper, the park is about
15km
away, or around
15–20 minutes
by vehicle. Use a tricycle or motorcycle taxi, and negotiate the fare.
A rental car or a car with a driver is the most comfortable option but costs more. Naga has several rental companies.
A PNR train route covering about
30km
from Naga to Libmanan in about
45 minutes

was featured in local media in October 2026. However, you would still need separate transport from the station to the cave park, so it is not a convenient option. Check PNR announcements for operating days and times.
Guides recommend visiting in the dry season, December–May, when there is less rain. Heavy rain can flood the caves, making them dangerous, and makes the entrance and access path slippery.
Check the weather forecast on the day of your visit, and postpone if there has been heavy rain in the past few days. It is safer to be out of the cave before sunset.

Few lodgings are near the park, so most visitors stay in Naga City and make a day trip. Naga is the center of Bicol and has many hotels, guesthouses, and restaurants. See the Naga City entry for details.

Libmanan town proper has small eateries and a market for lunch, but there is reportedly nothing for sale inside the park. It is safest to buy water, snacks, and a packed lunch beforehand. As is typical in Bicol, many dishes use coconut milk and chili, so tell the cook when ordering if you cannot take spicy food.

If a day trip is difficult, you could stay overnight in Libmanan town proper, but there is not much confirmed information about the number or quality of lodgings. The most reliable plan is to leave Naga, arrive in the morning, and return in the afternoon. After the cave, come back to Naga and enjoy Bicol cuisine. Sweat and dust will cover you in the cave, so bring a change of clothes and a towel.
Before you go, check with the Libmanan Tourism Office through its official page or contact details about whether the park is open, guides, and any permits. Some caves may require a DENR permit.
Always enter with a local guide. The cave is dark and the passages are complicated.
Wear sturdy shoes and avoid sandals. The ground is wet and uneven.
Bring a headlamp, a flashlight, and spare batteries. It is completely dark inside the cave.
Your phone may have no signal, so tell your lodging or family about your plans.
Bring water, snacks, a waterproof bag, trash bags, and cash in small bills, and take your trash out with you.
When photographing bats, avoid flash and use red light. Do not touch the bats or birds in the cave.
Leave early in the morning and plan to be back in town before sunset.
Wear clothes you do not mind getting wet and dirty, such as a long-sleeved top and long pants. Rock can scrape your elbows and knees.
Few visitors come to the park, so signage may be lacking. Do not rely on Google Maps alone; confirm the route with your guide or locals.
Information about this park's condition and whether it is open is conflicting. Be sure to check the latest status with the local tourism office and DENR before departing.
Some write-ups say fallen trees and inaccessible caves make a visit not recommended. Check ahead so you do not make the trip for nothing.
Some sections may be hard for people with claustrophobia, asthma, or joint problems, and for children and the elderly.
Caves can flood when it rains. Do not enter after heavy rain or during the rainy season.
Bat droppings cause odor and dust in the cave, and creatures such as spiders may live there, so gloves and a mask can help.
Stay with your group and follow only the marked paths. Do not go anywhere beyond your experience level.
The main city of central Bicol, with plenty of lodging and restaurants. Libmanan is about
1 hour
away by jeepney, making Naga a good base for visiting the caves.
A cold-water stream of about 20 small cascades in Barangay Bical, Libmanan, about
15km
from town proper. Confirm access and entry arrangements locally.
A small waterfall in Barangay Palong; resort admission is said to include the falls. Check the operating status locally.
